security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, when the vector execution unit processes vghsh.vs or vgmul.vs instructions, if the hardware does not check and trap on the condition where the vd register group overlaps the vs2 scalar element group (spec norm:vghsh-vs_vdovlpvs2_rsv and norm:vgmul-vs_vdovlpvs2_rsv), the scalar subkey H held in vs2 can be overwritten by partial result writes to vd before all element group iterations consume H. This creates a write-after-read hazard where later element groups use a corrupted hash subkey, producing incorrect GCM/GMAC authentication tags. The overlap check must consider VLEN-dependent EMUL: for VLEN >= 128, vs2 is a single register; for VLEN < 128, vs2 is a register group spanning ceil(128/VLEN) registers. The decoder or issue logic must raise an illegal-instruction exception when overlap is detected, per the spec's 'reserved encoding' classification.
security_spec.summary: Missing vd/vs2 register overlap trap on vghsh.vs/vgmul.vs allows scalar subkey corruption during GHASH, breaking GCM authentication and enabling forged ciphertext acceptance

findings.finding: vghsh.vs and vgmul.vs are NOT implemented in XiangShan RTL. The instructions file defines only Zvbb bit-patterns (VANDN_VV through VWSLL_VX). No Zvkg or Zvkgs BitPat objects exist. The only vector crypto extension implemented is Zvbb. vghsh.vv and vgmul.vv are also not implemented. Furthermore, the RISC-V specification (zvk.adoc lines 2631-2636, 2752-2757) explicitly states that .vs forms of vghsh and vgmul are NOT part of the current specification — they are listed as hypothetical 'future extension' possibilities in non-normative NOTE blocks. The generic .vs overlap constraint table (zvk.adoc lines 331-346) enumerates the instructions subject to vd/vs2 overlap checks and neither vghsh nor vgmul appear in that table. The normative rule tags cited in the security spec (norm:vghsh-vs_vdovlpvs2_rsv, norm:vgmul-vs_vdovlpvs2_rsv) do not exist in the current specification.

spec_citations.excerpt: NOTE: Since the same hash subkey H will typically be used repeatedly on a given message, a future extension might define a vector-scalar version of this instruction where vs2 is the scalar element group. This would help reduce register pressure when LMUL > 1.

NOTE: Since the same multiplicand will typically be used repeatedly on a given message, a future extension might define a vector-scalar version of this instruction where vs2 is the scalar element group. This would help reduce register pressure when LMUL > 1.
Table of .vs instructions where vd must not overlap vs2: vaes*.vs, vsm4r.vs, vsha2c[hl], vsha2ms, vsm3me, vsm3c. Neither vghsh nor vgmul appear in this table.

findings.finding: The notAllowOverlapInst exclusion list in VecExceptionGen does not include vghsh or vgmul. If these instructions were added in the future (either .vv or hypothetical .vs forms), the existing overlap-checking infrastructure would silently permit vd/vs2 overlap because vs2Constraint1 (EEW equality for non-mask instructions) would evaluate to true for these EEW=32 instructions, and the absence from notAllowOverlapInst means vs2AllowOverlap would be true. This is a defense-in-depth gap: the overlap detection logic has no forward-compatible safeguard for Zvkgs instructions that inherently require non-overlapping vd and vs2.
findings.snippet:
private val notAllowOverlapInst = lsIndexInst && inst.NF =/= 0.U || Seq(VMSBF_M, VMSIF_M, VMSOF_M, VIOTA_M,
    VSLIDEUP_VX, VSLIDEUP_VI, VSLIDE1UP_VX, VFSLIDE1UP_VF, VRGATHER_VV, VRGATHEREI16_VV, VRGATHER_VX, VRGATHER_VI, VCOMPRESS_VM).map(_ === inst.ALL).reduce(_ || _)

spec_citations.excerpt: For implementations with VLEN >= 128, vs2 refers to a single register. Thus, the vd register group must not overlap the vs2 register. However, in implementations where VLEN < 128, vs2 refers to a register group comprised of the number of registers needed to hold the 128-bit scalar element group. In this case, the vd register group must not overlap this vs2 register group.
